source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Electrical-Body and Chassis, p.12-3

procedures.title: Fusible links: locations and service
steps: Battery charging circuit link (Corvette): it is a molded splice at the solenoid "Bat" terminal; repair by splicing in a new link.
Horn relay link (16 gauge, black, protects all unfused 12-gauge-or-larger wiring): unplug the in-line connector and replace the link; it is not part of the harness.
Generator warning light and field circuit link (20 gauge, orange, in the battery feed to regulator #3 terminal wire): splice in a new 20 gauge wire.
Ammeter circuit links (two, 20 gauge, orange; at the solenoid "Bat" terminal on Corvette and at the horn relay): splice in new 20 gauge wire as needed.
notes: On models other than Corvette the charging-circuit link is a 14 gauge brown pigtail built into the battery positive cable, protecting the 10 gauge charging circuit.
Harness wires follow a color code common to all Chevrolets; composite wiring diagrams are figs. 89 to 110 at the end of the section.

procedures.title: Lighting and wiring maintenance
steps: Check now and then that all wiring connections are clean and tight and that lamps are mounted firmly for a good ground.
Replace any harness whose insulation is burned, cracked or deteriorated.
Solder every splice or broken-wire repair using rosin flux solder, then cover splices and bare wire with insulating tape.
Never substitute a wire of smaller gauge than the original.
Secure every harness and wire with clips so vibration cannot chafe the insulation.
Test circuits for continuity or shorts with a test lamp or low-reading voltmeter, using the wiring diagrams.
notes: Loose or corroded connections can cause a run-down battery, hard starting, dim lamps and generator/regulator damage.

procedures.title: Headlamp aiming with T-3 Safety Aimer (Type B)
steps: Caution: first check and tighten the radiator support and grille bolts; on Corvette, confirm the headlamp panel is adjusted correctly (see Headlamp Panel Adjustment).
Prepare the car: full fuel, oil and coolant, no load, tires at recommended pressure.
Drive onto the chosen aiming area, bounce the car several times and let it settle.
Take off the headlamp bezels if needed.
Fit the aimers on either the No. 1 or No. 2 pair of lamps so the lamp aiming points sit in the smooth inner ring of each aimer.
Press the center knob of each aimer firmly to lock it on (see figure 3 in the manual), then swing the crossarms inboard to roughly horizontal.
Knot both ends of the elastic string and hook it through the slots across both horizontal crossarms.
Rotate both aimers until the string just clears the crossarm points.
Horizontal: turn the horizontal aiming screw on the left lamp (see figure 4 in the manual) until the string sits over the crossarm centerline...
notes: In a dual headlamp system the inboard lamp is No. 1 and the outboard lamp is No. 2.
Wet the suction cups slightly for best grip.
Chevy II and Camaro 7-inch lamps need an adapter with the Type B aimer.
